note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001, CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001, or CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE retrieve/write/recall run.ids.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing hunt, expected shape, meaning, limitations. Path B is an answer key, not policy.

investigations.title: Find the experiment runs
investigations.security_question: Which run.ids belong to this incident, and are they LIVE or REPLAY?
investigations.learning_objective: Locate retrieve, write, and recall run.ids. Do not collapse three related runs into one UUID. Completeness is not proven by finding one id.
prerequisites: Attack Service launch or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Start from Q-RUN-EVENTS. Paste each quoted agentsec.run.id. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Capstone launches mint three UUIDs: RETRIEVE, WRITE, later RECALL. Attack Service Search handoff already ORs them.
investigations.hint_2: Finding events does not prove prevention, SAFE, or that Studio launched the run. LIVE ids are not the Investigate dropdown.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Three distinct run.ids per experiment. schema.version 1.9.0. testbed.mode BASELINE, ATTACK, or RETEST.
investigations.result_explanation: Each HTTP contract keeps its own run.id. Retrieve is RAG. Write is memory persist. Recall is later load plus MCP.
investigations.security_interpretation: Run.id is correlation, not authorization. Splunk reconstructed copies of telemetry.
investigations.does_not_prove: Finding the runs does not prove completeness, prevention, or that retrieved content granted a tool.

investigations.title: Reconstruct chronological execution
investigations.security_question: What happened, in runtime sequence order?
investigations.learning_objective: Order retrieve, memory write, later recall, control.decision, and mcp.* using agentsec.sequence, not _time as authority.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep all three run.ids. Sort by agentsec.sequence within each run, then chain retrieve → write → recall by launch order.
investigations.hint_1: Q-RUN-EVENTS tables sequence, event.name, hop_index. Memory written is on the write run. Recalled and MCP are on the recall run.
investigations.hint_2: _time order is not authoritative. Missing a hop is not prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Retrieve control OBSERVE, then memory.written, then memory.recalled, then MCP control, then maybe mcp.started.
investigations.result_explanation: The chain is SOURCE → fixture-equivalent persistence → later recall → request → authorization → invocation → completion/failure → outcome.
investigations.security_interpretation: Sequence reconstruction is CONTEXT. It does not decide ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.does_not_prove: A reconstructed timeline does not prove the retrieved document granted customer:read.

investigations.title: Identify retrieved source
investigations.security_question: What untrusted bytes entered as retrieved content?
investigations.learning_objective: Find document.id, content.hash, preview, and CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 on the retrieve run. Untrusted is not malicious.
investigations.starter_guidance: Bind Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY to the RETRIEVE run.id. Read context_document_id, context_hash, context_trust, context_decision.
investigations.hint_1: document.id is doc.lending-policy.normal on BASELINE and doc.lending-policy.malicious on ATTACK/RETEST.
investigations.hint_2: Preview is privacy-bounded. Hash is the fingerprint. Provenance rag.local.fixture is source identity, not trust.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One RAG OBSERVE row. context_trust untrusted_data. followon_tool empty on retrieve because capstone skips retrieve follow-on.
investigations.result_explanation: Retrieved content entered as data. This retrieve run did not execute lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.does_not_prove: Identifying the source does not prove it granted a tool or that it persisted.

investigations.title: Determine provenance and trust
investigations.security_question: Was the retrieved content trusted, and what provenance labeled it?
investigations.learning_objective: Separate provenance from trust. rag.local.fixture is not a grant. untrusted_data is classification, not malice.
investigations.starter_guidance: On the same RAG hunt, read context_provenance and context_trust. Confirm CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 decision is OBSERVE.
investigations.hint_1: PROVENANCE != TRUST. Known fixture provenance does not make content trusted instruction.
investigations.hint_2: Do not teach trust known provenance as the defense. Defense is authorization, not a whitelist of hashes.
investigations.expected_result_shape: context_provenance rag.local.fixture. context_trust untrusted_data. context_decision OBSERVE. derived_authority absent on retrieve.
investigations.result_explanation: The classifier recorded data. It did not ALLOW lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.security_interpretation: Trust labels are context. They are not coded_policy grants.
investigations.does_not_prove: OBSERVE does not mean SAFE. Untrusted does not mean the attack succeeded.

investigations.title: Determine whether equivalent content persisted
investigations.security_question: Did the memory store load fixture-equivalent bytes with the same canonical hash?
investigations.learning_objective: Compare retrieve content.hash to memory write content.hash. Schema 1.9.0 has no retrieve-to-write field; hash equality is an equality join, not proof of a direct copy.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the retrieve hash. On the WRITE run find event.name=agentsec.memory.written. Compare hashes. Do not invent a new field.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY write_hash should equal the RAG context_hash when the frozen object was used.
investigations.hint_2: Matching preview text is not the fingerprint. A schema bump was not authorized for this join.
investigations.expected_result_shape: write_hash equals retrieve context_hash. memory.id mem.capstone.retrieved.malicious on ATTACK/RETEST.
investigations.result_explanation: The memory store loaded fixture-equivalent RAG-001 bytes and the canonical hashes match. Hash equality proves equality of the compared bytes, not a direct retrieve-output → persist copy. Persistence is not a grant.
investigations.security_interpretation: STORED != TRUSTED. Persistence is an influence plane, not authority.
investigations.does_not_prove: A matching hash does not prove memory granted lookup_customer_tier.

investigations.title: Link memory WRITE to later RECALL
investigations.security_question: Which write run produced the later recall that still carries those bytes?
investigations.learning_objective: Prove write_run_id != recall_run_id and recall_source_run_id equals write_run_id. Same memory.id and hash.
investigations.starter_guidance: Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY with WRITE and RECALL tokens. Confirm write_recall_linked=linked.
investigations.hint_1: source_run_id on recall is the write UUID. Do not invent session.id.
investigations.hint_2: Linked persistence is not trust and is not authorization.
investigations.expected_result_shape: write_recall_linked linked. fingerprint_survived same_sha256. recall_source_run_id equals write_run_id.
investigations.result_explanation: A later run loaded the stored bytes. Cross-run reconstruction uses existing 1.9.0 fields.
investigations.security_interpretation: RECALLED != AUTHORIZED. Cross-run linkage is CONTEXT evidence.
investigations.does_not_prove: Linkage does not prove the memory granted a tool or that Goal Integrity failed.

investigations.title: Determine what recalled memory influenced
investigations.security_question: Did recalled memory shape a later privileged tool request?
investigations.learning_objective: Find follow-on tool lookup_customer_tier after MEMORY OBSERVE. Influence is not a grant.
investigations.starter_guidance: On Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY read followon_tool, followon_requested_scope, memory_decision. Confirm memory_decision OBSERVE.
investigations.hint_1: The closed interpreter recognizes the persisted RAG AGENT NOTE marker. The tool name is not taken from attacker grammar.
investigations.expected_result_shape: memory_decision OBSERVE memory_context_is_data. followon_tool lookup_customer_tier. followon_requested_scope customer:read on ATTACK/RETEST. BASELINE has no privileged follow-on.
investigations.result_explanation: Recalled bytes influenced a request object. CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 still OBSERVEd.
investigations.security_interpretation: A request can be formed without a grant. The PDP has not spoken yet.
investigations.does_not_prove: A follow-on request does not prove the memory granted customer:read.

investigations.title: Determine the requested privileged operation
investigations.security_question: What tool, scope, and resource were requested after recall?
investigations.learning_objective: Read gen_ai.tool.name, requested_scope, and resource from MCP rows on the recall run. REQUEST != GRANT.
investigations.starter_guidance: Reuse Q-MCP-WHO or Q-MCP-TOOL against the RECALL run.id. Look for lookup_customer_tier / customer:read / cust-001.
investigations.hint_1: BASELINE should not request lookup_customer_tier. ATTACK and RETEST should request the same privileged operation.
investigations.hint_2: Requested is not granted. Caller id is not a grant.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK/RETEST: lookup_customer_tier, customer:read, cust-001 on the recall run. BASELINE: no such request.
investigations.result_explanation: The later request is the influence result. Authorization is the next question.
investigations.security_interpretation: REQUEST != GRANT. The object evaluated for influence is the object used to request the tool.
investigations.does_not_prove: Seeing the request does not prove it executed or that RAG granted it.

investigations.title: Determine actual coded authority
investigations.security_question: What did coded_policy grant to the acting agent?
investigations.learning_objective: Read allowed_scope versus requested_scope. lookup_customer_tier / customer:read is not globally granted.
investigations.starter_guidance: Q-MCP-AUTHZ on the recall run. Compare requested_scope with allowed_scope. Coded tools remain lookup_policy.
investigations.hint_1: Vulnerable ATTACK overlay is per-experiment lab fail-open. It is not a mutation of coded_policy().
investigations.hint_2: CALLER ID != GRANT. Overlay reason is not a production IOC.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Coded allowed_scope remains policy:read. Requested customer:read. ATTACK decision ALLOW with labeled fail-open. RETEST DENY tool_not_granted.
investigations.result_explanation: Global policy did not grow a customer:read grant. The ATTACK ALLOW is a labeled lab overlay on that recall run only.
investigations.security_interpretation: Authority enters at CTRL-MCP-001. RAG and memory did not mint the grant.
investigations.does_not_prove: An ALLOW row does not prove coded_policy changed. It does not prove execution.

investigations.title: Determine which control made the authorization decision
investigations.security_question: Which control authorized or denied the privileged tool?
investigations.learning_objective: Two classifier OBSERVE rows may appear. Only CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP. OBSERVE != ALLOW.
investigations.starter_guidance: Q-MCP-AUTHZ plus the RAG/memory hunts. Name the control.id on the tool decision hop.
investigations.hint_1: CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 and CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 stay OBSERVE on ATTACK and RETEST.
investigations.hint_2: Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY. Attack Service did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Tool hop control.id CTRL-MCP-001. Classifiers OBSERVE. ATTACK ALLOW. RETEST DENY tool_not_granted.
investigations.result_explanation: The authorization decision is the MCP control. Influence planes classified data.
investigations.security_interpretation: SOLE TOOL PDP = CTRL-MCP-001. SPLUNK != ENFORCEMENT.
investigations.does_not_prove: Naming the PDP does not prove the handler ran. ALLOW != EXECUTION.

investigations.title: Determine whether execution occurred
investigations.learning_objective: Separate request, ALLOW/DENY, ToolRegistry invocation, mcp.completed/mcp.failed, and application outcome. The process-local count proves invocation began, not successful completion. Missing mcp.started is not prevention proof.
investigations.starter_guidance: Q-MCP-EXECUTED and Q-MCP-TOOL on the recall run. Compare with Attack Service handler count.
investigations.hint_1: ATTACK expected handler 1 and mcp.started. RETEST expected handler 0 and no mcp.started on a complete copy.
investigations.hint_2: MISSING EVENT != PREVENTION. DENY != proof of non-execution without execution evidence. ALLOW != EXECUTION.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK: ToolRegistry invocation count 1, mcp.started, mcp.completed, successful hop/outcome. RETEST: invocation count 0 and no indexed follow-on execution event on a complete copy.
investigations.result_explanation: Execution is a handler invocation. Telemetry copies that fact when export is complete.
investigations.security_interpretation: ToolRegistry count is invocation-begin evidence. mcp.completed or mcp.failed plus hop/outcome distinguishes completion from failure. Splunk is reconstructed telemetry.
investigations.does_not_prove: Missing mcp.started alone does not prove the handler did not run.

investigations.title: Is Goal Integrity required to explain the event?
investigations.security_question: Must a Goal Integrity failure be present to explain this incident?
investigations.learning_objective: Test whether Goal Integrity telemetry is present. Zero Q-GOAL-INTEGRITY-AUTHORITY rows means CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 is NOT PRESENT in this packet. Instrumented absence is not proof the domain never fails.
investigations.starter_guidance: Run Q-GOAL-INTEGRITY-AUTHORITY on retrieve, write, and recall ids. Expect zero rows in this instrumented experiment.
investigations.hint_1: This capstone does not activate Goal Integrity as a vulnerability. AUTHORIZED TOOL != AUTHORIZED GOAL remains a true rule, but it is not the incident mechanism here.
investigations.hint_2: Do not teach no event means it definitely did not happen anywhere. Teach the limits of the instrumented experiment.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Zero rows for these run.ids. TASK / GOAL FAILURE: NOT PRESENT IN THIS PACKET.
investigations.result_explanation: No CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 row is indexed for this packet. You do not need a goal failure to explain customer-tier access here.
investigations.security_interpretation: Ruling out a domain is a security-reasoning skill. Zero rows here are instrumented absence, not a universal guarantee.
investigations.does_not_prove: Zero goal rows do not prove Goal Integrity can never fail, that extract_full_policy never occurs, or that the application is safe.

investigations.title: Is Identity/Delegation required to explain the event?
investigations.security_question: Must an Identity or Delegation failure be present to explain this incident?
investigations.learning_objective: Test whether Identity telemetry is present. Zero Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY rows means CTRL-IDENTITY-001 is NOT PRESENT in this packet. WHO AUTHENTICATED remains NOT PROVEN because no auth stack exists.
investigations.starter_guidance: Run Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY on the same three run.ids. Expect zero rows.
investigations.hint_1: IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION still holds as a rule. This incident is not a claim incident.
investigations.hint_2: No event does not mean identity never matters. It means this experiment did not emit that family.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Zero rows. IDENTITY / DELEGATION FAILURE: NOT PRESENT IN THIS PACKET.
investigations.result_explanation: No CTRL-IDENTITY-001 row is indexed. You do not need a delegation claim to explain this customer-tier access.
investigations.security_interpretation: Do not blame every agent-security mechanism. Name the planes that actually have evidence.
investigations.does_not_prove: Zero identity rows do not prove authentication, SPIFFE, OAuth, or that impersonation is impossible.

investigations.title: Compare ATTACK and RETEST
investigations.security_question: What changed when defense changed, given equivalent adversarial bytes?
investigations.learning_objective: SAME influence (hash, memory, requested tool). DIFFERENT ExperimentContext, MCP decision, execution, and run.ids.
investigations.starter_guidance: Reuse Q-MCP-AUTHZ on each recall run.id. Confirm ATTACK and RETEST content.hash MATCH. Do not infer equivalence from fixture names.
investigations.hint_1: Primary statement: SAME ADVERSARIAL INFLUENCE. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION.
investigations.hint_2: One RETEST is not universal resistance. BASELINE is not SAFE. Colors are not proof.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Same hash. ATTACK ALLOW + handler 1. RETEST DENY tool_not_granted + handler 0. RAG/memory still OBSERVE.
investigations.result_explanation: Defense removed the lab overlay. Influence remained. Authorization and execution changed.
investigations.security_interpretation: Splunk observed the difference. Splunk did not cause it. Influence can remain present without becoming authority.
investigations.does_not_prove: RETEST does not prove the application is secure against all RAG/memory attacks.

investigations.title: Identify the real enforcement point
investigations.learning_objective: Enforcement is AcmeBank CTRL-MCP-001 before the handler. Not RAG. Not memory. Not Splunk. Not Attack Service. Not learning metadata.
investigations.starter_guidance: Name the control.id on the tool hop. Confirm classifiers stayed OBSERVE. Confirm Splunk has no deny action.
investigations.hint_1: Do not teach sanitize everything, delete memory, block all RAG, or trust known provenance as the defense that changed RETEST.
investigations.hint_2: HEC ACCEPTANCE != SEARCHABLE EVIDENCE. Overlay is lab fail-open.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Enforcement = CTRL-MCP-001. Classifiers OBSERVE. Splunk reconstructs.
investigations.result_explanation: The defended experiment kept adversarial influence and removed the lab overlay.
investigations.security_interpretation: SPLUNK != ENFORCEMENT. RAG != PDP. MEMORY != PDP.
investigations.does_not_prove: Identifying the PDP does not prove universal resistance or that missing telemetry is prevention.

investigations.title: Classify what the evidence proves
investigations.security_question: What can you prove, corroborate, leave unproven, or mark incorrect?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify statements as SUPPORTED, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT. ToolRegistry count proves invocation began; completion/failure and outcome require additional runtime evidence. CTRL-MCP-001 is authorization. Splunk is reconstructed telemetry.
investigations.starter_guidance: For each claim, pick one class. Do not upgrade expected results into measured results. Do not treat Path B as policy.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED examples: CTRL-MCP-001 authorized the ATTACK tool; ToolRegistry invocation count is 1; mcp.completed plus success supports completion/outcome; RETEST per-run invocation count is 0. CORROBORATED: indexed mcp.started on a complete ATTACK copy.
investigations.hint_2: INCORRECT: The retrieved document granted customer:read. The memory record granted lookup_customer_tier. Splunk prevented the attack. RETEST proves the application is secure against all RAG/memory attacks. Missing telemetry proves prevention. NOT PROVEN: WHO AUTHENTICATED; universal resistance; that Goal/Identity never fail.
investigations.expected_result_shape: A classified claim list. Handler counts from runtime. Splunk rows labeled corroboration. No DET-CAPSTONE.
investigations.result_explanation: Proof classes keep evidence honest. Studio Path B is an answer key.
investigations.security_interpretation: ToolRegistry count = invocation began, not completion. mcp.completed / mcp.failed + hop/outcome = terminal runtime evidence. CTRL-MCP-001 = authorization. Splunk = reconstructed telemetry. RAG/memory OBSERVE = classification. Splunk != enforcement. One RETEST != universal resistance.
investigations.does_not_prove: Completing Path B does not prove the learner launched LIVE, that HEC rows are searchable, or that the product is production-safe.
